issues.description: Animal.name attribute type is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement text (problem_statement.md) explicitly instructs students to use a StringBuilder for the Animal.name attribute, while the UML in the same problem statement shows the attribute as type String (name: String). The reference solution (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) implements the field as private String name. This three-way mismatch (text vs. UML vs. solution) creates ambiguity for students about the correct type to implement, affects constructor/getter/setter signatures and expected return types for uses of getName() in Pig/Goat/Seal, and may lead to unnecessary confusion or compile/runtime friction when students try to follow the textual guidance.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and reference implementation consistent. Two practical options: (A) If the exercise intends to teach use of StringBuilder, update the UML and the reference solution: change Animal.java to use private StringBuilder name; update the constructor to initialize the StringBuilder (e.g., this.name = new StringBuilder(nameParam)); provide getName() that returns a String (return name.toString()) or a getNameBuilder() that returns the StringBuilder while keeping getName() returning String to avoid breaking existing callers; update Pig/Seal/Goat usages to call getName() as needed. Or (B) if the exercise does not actually require StringBuilder, remove the StringBuilder requirement from the problem text (and/or the UML) and keep the field as String in the solution. Prefer one clear approach and apply it to the problem text (both UML and prose) and the reference solution so students have an unambiguous requirement.
